page: Microsoft Azure D2pls_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache specifications consist of 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates modest performance characteristics. Single-core processing shows average capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1822.08 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 24.13 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are limited. The stress-ng multi-core test scored 3617.67, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 1903.0, both falling into the lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block read and write speeds of 22.77 GB/sec and 14.05 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2pls_v5 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 computing on Azure, trading off high memory capacity and raw multi-threaded performance for dedicated physical cores at a lower resource density. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, minor database operations, or simple microservices and development environments that do not require extensive memory or high-speed local storage.
